name: cube
description: A box with one corner at the origin, or centred when center=true. size is a number (cube) or a [x, y, z] vector.
arguments: center = true centres the box on the origin. Default false
examples: translate([0, 0, 3]) cube([30, 20, 6], center=true);  // bottom on z = 0

name: sphere
description: A sphere centred on the origin. Use $fn (or $fa/$fs) to control facets; a low-facet sphere measures under-size across flats.
examples: sphere(d=10, $fn=48);

name: cylinder
description: A cylinder from z = 0 to z = h (or centred with center=true). Give r/d for a cylinder, r1,r2 or d1,d2 for a cone. Facets come from $fn (exact count), or $fa/$fs. For bores and bosses that are measured, set $fn on the primitive (96–160) and remember a polygon inscribed in the circle is under-size by r·(1 − cos(180/$fn)); the checker fits a circle to the polygon vertices, so 96+ facets keep that below 0.03 mm at 40 mm.
arguments: r1, r2 | d1, d2 = bottom and top radii/diameters (cone)
center = centre on z = 0. Default false
examples: cylinder(h=6, d=43.25, $fn=128);
cylinder(h=10, d1=12, d2=8, $fn=64);  // taper
difference() { cylinder(h=6, d=54, $fn=128); translate([0,0,-1]) cylinder(h=8, d=43.25, $fn=128); }  // ring

name: polyhedron
synopsis: Arbitrary closed mesh from points and faces.
description: A solid from a list of vertices and faces (lists of point indices). Faces must be ordered clockwise when looking at the face from outside, and the surface must be closed and consistently oriented or the result is not a valid 2-manifold. Prefer linear_extrude/rotate_extrude of a polygon, hull(), or BOSL2 sweeps; reach for polyhedron only for lofts you cannot express otherwise.
arguments: faces = [[i, j, k, ...], ...] indices into points, clockwise from outside

name: import
synopsis: Load an external STL/DXF/SVG (not available in Kintsugi sessions).
description: Imports a mesh or 2D file. Kintsugi parts must be self-contained: no import() unless the spec supplies the file. The checker measures the exported mesh, so an imported blob would be unverifiable anyway.

name: surface
synopsis: Height map from a data file or PNG (not used here).
description: Reads a height map. Not applicable to Kintsugi parts.

name: square
description: A rectangle with one corner at the origin, or centred. 2D shapes are extruded with linear_extrude/rotate_extrude; a 2D object left at top level exports as a thin 1 mm slab (avoid).
examples: linear_extrude(6) square([30, 20], center=true);

name: circle
description: A circle as a regular polygon with $fn sides (or per $fa/$fs). The polygon is inscribed: its flats sit inside the true circle by r·(1 − cos(180/$fn)). Use $fn ≥ 96 for measured bores; 128–180 for press fits.
examples: linear_extrude(6) difference() { circle(d=54, $fn=128); circle(d=43.25, $fn=128); }

name: polygon
synopsis: 2D shape from a point list, with optional holes.
description: A polygon from [x, y] points in order (either winding). paths lists index loops: the first is the outline, the rest are holes. Self-intersecting outlines produce broken extrusions — build the outline from simple pieces and union them instead. This is the workhorse for measured outlines and profiles: build the profile as points, then linear_extrude (flat parts) or rotate_extrude (round parts).
examples:
// L profile revolved into a flanged ring
rotate_extrude($fn=128) polygon([[21.6,0],[27,0],[27,3],[24,3],[24,8],[21.6,8]]);

// hook outline from a point list
linear_extrude(4) polygon([[0,0],[20,0],[20,4],[4,4],[4,30],[0,30]]);

name: text
usage: text("str", size=10, font=, halign="left", valign="baseline", spacing=1, direction="ltr", $fn=);
description: Outline glyphs in the XY plane; extrude to emboss or difference to engrave. size is roughly the cap height in mm. Fonts must exist on the machine; the default sans works everywhere. Keep embossed text ≥ 0.6 mm tall and 0.4–1 mm raised for FDM; engraved text 0.6–1 mm deep.
arguments: size = nominal size (≈ ascender height) in mm. Default 10
examples: difference() { cube([40, 12, 3]); translate([2, 3, 2.2]) linear_extrude(1) text("KIN", size=7); }
notes: textmetrics() does not exist in 2021.01 (it returns undef); size text by trial, or leave margin.

name: offset
synopsis: Grow/shrink a 2D shape; rounds or chamfers corners.
description: Offsets a 2D shape by a distance. r rounds the corners (outward offset rounds convex corners; a negative r rounds concave corners and removes features thinner than 2|r|). delta keeps corners sharp (chamfer=true cuts them). The standard rounding idiom: offset(r=+R) offset(delta=-R) rounds convex corners of radius R without changing size; offset(r=-R) offset(delta=+R) rounds concave (inside) corners. Both together round everything. Use on the 2D profile before extruding — far cheaper than minkowski.
arguments: r = offset distance with rounded corners
delta = offset distance with sharp corners
chamfer = with delta, chamfer the corners instead of extending them
examples:
// 3 mm rounded outside corners, size unchanged
linear_extrude(4) offset(r=3) offset(delta=-3) square([40, 20]);

// fillet the inside corners of an L
linear_extrude(4) offset(r=-2) offset(delta=2) polygon([[0,0],[30,0],[30,8],[8,8],[8,30],[0,30]]);

name: projection
description: Projects a 3D object onto the XY plane. cut=false gives the silhouette (union of all sections); cut=true gives the section at z = 0 only — translate first to cut at another height. Useful for turning a body into a 2D outline to offset (a gasket, a lid that matches a base).
arguments: cut = false: silhouette; true: section at z = 0
examples:
linear_extrude(2) offset(r=1) projection() import_free_body();
module import_free_body() cylinder(h=10, d=20, $fn=64);

name: linear_extrude
synopsis: Extrude a 2D shape along Z (optionally twist/scale).
usage: linear_extrude(height, center=false, convexity=10, twist=0, slices=, scale=1) ...2D;
description: Turns a 2D shape into a prism from z = 0 to height (centred with center=true). twist rotates the profile over the height (degrees), scale shrinks/grows it (number or [x, y]); slices controls the segmentation of twisted/scaled extrusions. convexity only affects preview rendering; the exported STL is exact. This plus polygon/offset is the cleanest way to build flat repair parts: model the outline in 2D, round it with offset, extrude the thickness.
arguments: twist = degrees of rotation over the height
scale = top scale factor (number or [x, y]); 0 makes a point
examples: linear_extrude(6) offset(r=2) offset(delta=-2) square([40, 20], center=true);
linear_extrude(15, scale=0.8, $fn=64) circle(d=20);  // tapered plug

name: rotate_extrude
description: Revolves a 2D shape drawn in the XY plane around the Z axis: X becomes the radius, Y becomes Z. The profile must lie entirely at x ≥ 0 (or entirely ≤ 0). angle < 360 makes a partial revolve (arcs, snap-ring gaps). Ideal for rings, caps, knobs, bushings, flanges: draw the cross-section as a polygon and revolve. $fn on rotate_extrude sets the facets around the axis.
examples:
// ring: OD 54, bore 43.25, height 6, with a 1 mm chamfer at the bore entry
rotate_extrude($fn=128) polygon([[21.625+1,0],[27,0],[27,6],[21.625,6],[21.625,1]]);

// knob with a rounded rim
rotate_extrude($fn=96) { square([12, 8]); translate([12, 4]) circle(r=4, $fn=32); }

name: translate
description: Moves the children by a vector. Transforms apply to everything that follows in the same statement or block.
arguments: v = [x, y, z] (2D children take [x, y])
examples: translate([0, 0, 6]) cube(10);

name: rotate
description: Rotates children by Euler angles in degrees, applied X then Y then Z, about the origin — translate afterwards, or rotate about a point with translate(p) rotate(a) translate(-p). rotate(a, v) rotates about an arbitrary axis vector. A single number rotates about Z (2D and 3D).
arguments: a = angle or [ax, ay, az] in degrees
examples: rotate([90, 0, 0]) cylinder(h=20, d=6, $fn=48);  // horizontal hole along -Y

name: scale
description: Scales children about the origin. Non-uniform scale of a circle gives an ellipse (facets are scaled too). Scaling a rounded shape scales its radii — use offset/BOSL2 rounding for true constant radii.
examples: scale([1, 0.6, 1]) cylinder(h=6, d=40, $fn=96);  // oval boss

name: resize
synopsis: Scale children to an exact bounding size.
description: Scales children so their bounding box matches newsize. A 0 in newsize keeps that axis unscaled unless auto=true (then it scales proportionally). Forces geometry evaluation (slower).
arguments: newsize = [x, y, z]; 0 = unchanged (or proportional with auto)
examples: resize([50, 0, 0], auto=true) sphere(d=10);

name: mirror
synopsis: Mirror children across a plane through the origin.
description: Reflects children across the plane whose normal is the given vector. mirror does not keep the original — use a union of the shape and its mirror for symmetric parts: `module both() { children(); mirror([1,0,0]) children(); }`.
arguments: v = plane normal, e.g. [1,0,0] mirrors X
examples:
module both() { children(); mirror([1, 0, 0]) children(); }
both() translate([10, 0, 0]) cube(5);

name: multmatrix
description: Applies an arbitrary affine transform. Rarely needed by hand; BOSL2 provides shear/skew helpers.

name: color
description: Preview colour only; it does not affect the exported mesh. Useful in assembly() to tell the part from the ghosted context.
arguments: c = name string, [r,g,b] or [r,g,b,a] in 0–1, or "#rrggbb"
examples: color("steelblue") cube(10);

name: hull
description: The convex hull of all children — the fastest way to make rounded, tapered or lofted convex bodies: hull two spheres for a capsule, four cylinders for a rounded plate, two discs for a truncated cone with rounded ends. hull discards concavities, so build concave parts from several hulls unioned. Works in 2D too.
examples:
// rounded plate 40×20×4 with R3 corners
hull() for (x=[-17,17], y=[-7,7]) translate([x, y, 0]) cylinder(h=4, r=3, $fn=32);

// loop: two rings joined by a hull bridge
hull() { translate([0,0,0]) cylinder(h=6, d=54, $fn=96); translate([70,0,0]) cylinder(h=6, d=30, $fn=96); }

name: minkowski
synopsis: Minkowski sum of children (rounds every edge).
description: Sweeps the second child around the first: body + sphere(r) rounds all edges with radius r (and grows the body by r — model the body smaller). Correct but expensive (CGAL: seconds to minutes; cost grows with facets). Prefer offset() on 2D profiles, hull() of rounded primitives, or BOSL2 cuboid(rounding=) / rounded_prism(). If used, keep the sphere $fn low (16–24) and the body simple.
examples: minkowski() { cube([40-6, 20-6, 6-6+0.01], center=true); sphere(r=3, $fn=20); }

name: union
synopsis: Merge children into one solid (implicit at top level).
description: Combines children. Top-level statements are implicitly unioned. Overlap parts by a small epsilon (0.01–0.1 mm) rather than touching exactly — coincident faces make CGAL produce non-manifold results or slow renders.
examples: union() { cube(10); translate([9.99, 0, 0]) cube(10); }

name: difference
synopsis: Subtract every child after the first.
description: Keeps the first child minus all others. Make cutters overshoot the faces they exit (start them 1 mm below and end 1 mm above) so no coincident faces remain — the classic cause of 'Object may not be a valid 2-manifold' and of zero-thickness skins. Use `#` on a cutter to see it in preview.
examples: difference() { cylinder(h=6, d=54, $fn=128); translate([0, 0, -1]) cylinder(h=8, d=43.25, $fn=128); }

name: intersection
synopsis: Keep only the volume common to all children.
description: The overlap of all children. Handy to clip a shape to an envelope (a sphere intersected with a cube for a domed cap) or to bound a hull.
examples: intersection() { sphere(d=40, $fn=96); translate([0, 0, 10]) cube([50, 50, 20], center=true); }

name: intersection_for
synopsis: Intersection over a loop (for() would union).
description: Like for(), but the iterations are intersected instead of unioned. Used for shapes defined as the common volume of rotated copies (a rounded-triangle knob, a spherical cap set).
examples: intersection_for (a = [0, 60, 120]) rotate(a) cube([30, 8, 8], center=true);

name: render
synopsis: Force CGAL evaluation of children (preview only).
description: In preview (F5) it replaces the children with their computed mesh, fixing display artifacts of complex booleans. Headless STL export already evaluates everything; render() there only costs time. Not needed in Kintsugi parts.

name: for
synopsis: Repeat children over a range or list (results are unioned).
description: Instantiates the children once per value; the copies are unioned. Ranges are inclusive: [0:3] is 0,1,2,3; [0:0.5:2] steps by 0.5. Iterate a list of points for hole patterns. Use intersection_for to intersect instead.
examples: for (p = [[-25, 0], [25, 0]]) translate([p[0], p[1], -1]) cylinder(h=8, d=4.5, $fn=32);  // two clearance holes
for (i = [0:5]) rotate(i * 60) translate([20, 0, 0]) cylinder(h=4, d=3, $fn=24);  // bolt circle

name: if
description: Instantiates children when the condition holds. Conditions use ==, !=, <, <=, >, >=, &&, ||, !. undef and 0 are false-ish in boolean context (0 == false is true).
examples: if (with_lanyard_hole) translate([90, 0, -1]) cylinder(h=8, d=4, $fn=32);

name: let
synopsis: Local named values (statement and expression forms).
description: Binds names for the following children or expression. Variables in OpenSCAD cannot be reassigned; let is how you compute intermediates (derived dimensions, points) locally. Later bindings can use earlier ones.
examples:
let (ri = neck_d/2 + clearance, ro = ri + wall) rotate_extrude($fn=128) polygon([[ri,0],[ro,0],[ro,6],[ri,6]]);
neck_d = 43; clearance = 0.25; wall = 4;

name: echo
synopsis: Print values to the console (compile output).
description: Prints to the console; in Kintsugi the compile output shows it, so echo the derived dimensions you care about (bore diameter with clearance, wall thickness) and compare them with the check table. echo() as an expression also exists: echo(x) x.
examples:
echo(bore=neck_d + clearance, wall=(ring_od - neck_d - clearance)/2);
neck_d=43; clearance=0.25; ring_od=54;

name: assert
synopsis: Stop with a message when a condition fails.
description: Aborts the compile (an error in the output) when the condition is false. Put the spec's hard constraints in asserts at the top of part.scad so an impossible parameter combination fails loudly instead of producing a silently wrong part.
examples:
assert(loop_inner_w >= 40, "two fingers need 40 mm");
loop_inner_w = 42;

name: children
description: Inside a module, children() places the objects the caller passed in braces; $children is their count. This is how wrapper modules (both(), bed_chamfer(), pattern()) apply transforms to arbitrary geometry.
examples:
module ring_array(n, r) { for (i=[0:n-1]) rotate(i*360/n) translate([r,0,0]) children(); }
ring_array(6, 20) cylinder(h=4, d=3, $fn=24);

name: module
synopsis: Define a reusable geometry block with parameters.
description: Modules produce geometry; call them like primitives. Parameters have defaults; named arguments are allowed (`name(b=2)`). Modules see file-level variables. Keep Kintsugi's required modules: part(), coupon(), assembly().
examples:
module boss(d, h, hole) { difference() { cylinder(h=h, d=d, $fn=64); translate([0,0,-1]) cylinder(h=h+2, d=hole, $fn=48); } }
boss(10, 8, 4.5);

name: function
synopsis: Define an expression with parameters (recursion allowed).
description: Functions return values (numbers, lists, strings, booleans, function literals) and can recurse (ternary as the base case). Use them for profile points, derived dimensions and unit helpers. Function literals can be stored in variables and passed as arguments.

name: list comprehension
usage: [for (i = a) each [i, i+1]]  // flatten one level
description: The way to compute point lists, hole positions and derived tables. each splices a list into the result (2019.05+). Ranges are inclusive. Conditions filter; let computes intermediates. Nested fors with a comma iterate all combinations.
examples:
arc = [for (a = [0:5:90]) [20*cos(a), 20*sin(a)]];
linear_extrude(2) polygon(concat([[0,0]], arc));

holes = [for (x=[-30,30], y=[-15,15]) [x, y]];
difference() { cube([80,40,4], center=true); for (p=holes) translate([p[0],p[1],-3]) cylinder(h=8, d=3.4, $fn=24); }

name: variables
usage: name = expr;  // inside a module: local to that module
description: Variables are set once per scope, evaluated before the geometry, and cannot be reassigned in loops or conditionally; a repeated assignment at the same level makes the LAST one win for the whole scope (with a warning) — which is how -D overrides and the customizer work. Compute per-iteration values with let(), functions and list comprehensions. Order of statements does not matter for variables at the same level; undefined names are undef (a warning), not an error.

name: special variables
description: $-variables are dynamically scoped: setting one in a call ($fn=128) applies to that primitive and its children; setting it at the top applies everywhere. $fn overrides $fa/$fs. $preview is true in F5 preview and false in headless export (Kintsugi always exports, so $preview is false). $children is the child count in a module. $t is the animation time (unused).
examples:
$fn = 96;
cylinder(h=6, d=43.25, $fn=160);  // this bore gets more facets
notes: Facet cost: CGAL time grows with facet count; 96 for bodies and 128–160 for measured bores is a good budget in 2021.01.

name: modifier characters
description: Prefix modifiers. `%` (background) shows an object translucently in preview and excludes it from the exported mesh — Kintsugi's assembly() uses it to ghost the context proxies. `#` highlights a cutter for debugging (it is still part of the result). `!` renders only that subtree; `*` disables one.
examples: difference() { cube(20); #translate([5,5,-1]) cylinder(h=22, d=6, $fn=32); }

name: include
description: include pastes the file (its variables and top-level geometry become part of yours); use imports only its modules/functions. BOSL2 must be include'd (it needs its variables). The BOSL2 library is on OPENSCADPATH in every Kintsugi compile.
examples:
include <BOSL2/std.scad>
cuboid([30, 20, 6], rounding=2, edges="Z");

name: ternary and operators
synopsis: cond ? a : b, arithmetic, ^ power, vector ops.
description: The ternary is the only conditional expression; nest it for multi-way choices or use lookup(). Vectors add/subtract elementwise, scale by numbers, and `*` between vectors is the dot product (matrix products work too). Strings concatenate with str(). Integer division is float division; use floor(). `%` is modulo.
examples:
fit = clearance > 0.3 ? "loose" : "sliding"; echo(fit);
clearance = 0.25;

name: abs
description: Absolute value.

name: sin
description: All trig functions take and return DEGREES.

name: cos
description: Degrees.

name: tan
description: Degrees.

name: asin
description: Arcsine in degrees.

name: acos
description: Arccosine in degrees.

name: atan
description: Arctangent in degrees.

name: atan2
description: Angle of the vector [x, y] from the X axis; safe when x = 0.

name: floor
description: Round down.

name: ceil
description: Round up.

name: round
synopsis: Round to nearest (half away from zero).
description: Round to nearest (half away from zero).

name: sqrt
description: Square root.

name: pow
description: The ^ operator exists from 2021.01.

name: exp
description: e^x.

name: ln
description: Natural log.

name: log
description: Log base 10, or base b.

name: min
synopsis: Smallest of arguments or of a list.
description: Smallest of arguments or of a list.

name: max
synopsis: Largest of arguments or of a list.
description: Largest of arguments or of a list.

name: norm
description: Euclidean length of a vector.

name: cross
description: Cross product of 3-vectors.

name: len
synopsis: Length of a list or string.
description: undef for numbers.

name: concat
description: Lists only; to append an element wrap it: concat(list, [x]).

name: str
description: Numbers are formatted compactly (43.25 → "43.25").

name: chr
description: Character from code point(s).

name: ord
description: Code point of a character.

name: search
description: Returns indices; quirky — prefer a list comprehension with if for clarity.

name: lookup
description: Interpolates between the surrounding keys; clamps outside the table. Good for fit clearance by diameter or wall count by load.

name: rands
description: Give a seed for repeatable geometry (textures, knurls).

name: is_undef
description: Also is_list, is_num, is_string, is_bool, is_function (2021.01).

name: version
description: Kintsugi runs 2021.01.

name: not available in 2021.01
synopsis: Features you may remember that do not exist here.
usage: import() of files → disallowed in sessions
description: OpenSCAD 2021.01 is the stable release Kintsugi ships. Anything from later development snapshots (roof, textmetrics, Manifold, `--enable=` experimental features, object literals) is not available. Vanilla features available: function literals, ^, is_function, each, let, assert, echo expressions, offset chamfer, rotate_extrude angle, text, projection cut, $preview. The vendored BOSL2 (2.0.759) works on 2021.01 as tested here (threads, screws, attachments, sweeps, masks, hinges, gears).
